```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4.8,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

This article assumes the [introduction](introduction-to-interact.html),
especially Sections 2 and 5. It follows one comparison and asks how the
combined effect and the interaction become the two grey diamonds on a
CAMS forest. The fitting tutorial is not repeated.

## 1. One comparison on the forest

Section 5 of the introduction draws three marks for each subgroup. The
black square is the published subgroup estimate. The grey diamond is
that comparison's subgroup shrinkage estimate. The pooled diamond is
the mean subgroup effect at the reporting information fraction. The
grey diamond and the pooled diamond answer different questions.

The comparison here is ADVANCE in `age`: relapse on treatment versus
control, for younger and older patients, on the log incidence-rate-ratio
scale. Younger patients are the reference subgroup. The half-normal
priors are the ones used in the introduction, scale 0.5 for the
combined-effect heterogeneity and scale 0.1 for the interaction
heterogeneity. They are not the package defaults.

```{r fit-advance}
library(interact)

fit <- cams(
  age,
  reference = "Younger",
  tau.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.5),
  tau.interaction.prior = function(tau) bayesmeta::dhalfnormal(tau, scale = 0.1)
)
```

## 2. The published pair as a combined effect and an interaction

Section 2 of the introduction re-expresses the two published estimates.
With the younger subgroup as group A and the older subgroup as group B,

$$
g_j = y_{Bj} - y_{Aj},
$$

$$
m_j = (1 - \pi_j)\, y_{Aj} + \pi_j\, y_{Bj}.
$$

$\pi_j$ is the older subgroup's share of the precision in this
comparison. It is not the proportion of older patients. The table
evaluates both expressions at ADVANCE's published estimates.

```{r advance-pair}
trial <- "ADVANCE"
adv_row <- age[age$trial == trial, ]
y_A <- adv_row$yi[adv_row$subgroup == "Younger"]
y_B <- adv_row$yi[adv_row$subgroup == "Older"]
adv_q <- cams_trial_quantities(fit)
adv_q <- adv_q[adv_q$trial == trial, ]
pi_j <- adv_q$pi
m_obs <- adv_q$m
g_obs <- adv_q$g
stopifnot(abs(g_obs - (y_B - y_A)) < 1e-8)
stopifnot(abs(m_obs - ((1 - pi_j) * y_A + pi_j * y_B)) < 1e-8)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    quantity = c(
      "Younger, y_A",
      "Older, y_B",
      "Information fraction",
      "Combined effect, m",
      "Interaction, g"
    ),
    value = c(y_A, y_B, pi_j, m_obs, g_obs)
  ),
  digits = 3
)
```

## 3. The joint on square axes

`shrinkage()` summarizes a posterior for the combined effect and a
posterior for the interaction. Under the fitted model those two
components are independent, so the joint posterior is the product of
the two densities. That product is a statement about the two
components. It is separate from the conditional sampling independence
of the published subgroup estimates, which Section 2 of the
introduction uses to separate $m_j$ and $g_j$ in the likelihood.

The left panel draws that product. The square is the published pair
$(m_j, g_j)$ from the table. The diamond is the pair of posterior
medians. Dashed lines are values of the younger-subgroup effect
$m - \pi_j g$. The solid line is the published younger estimate. One
unit on the horizontal axis has the same length as one unit on the
vertical axis, so the slope of those lines is the slope of
$m - \pi_j g$.

The right panel is the same posterior written in the subgroup
coordinates

$$
\mu_A = m - \pi_j g, \qquad \mu_B = m + (1 - \pi_j)\, g.
$$

The square is the published pair $(y_A, y_B)$. The diamond is the pair
of posterior medians of the two subgroup effects, the numbers Section 4
prints. The level sets that slope on the left are vertical on the
right, because the horizontal axis is the younger-subgroup effect. The
axes are again square.

```{r joint-fig, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Posteriors of ADVANCE's comparison-specific combined effect and interaction. Left: that joint distribution. Right: the same distribution for the two subgroup effects; its medians are the subgroup-specific shrinkage estimates. Squares are published values. Diamonds are posterior medians. Dashed lines are level sets of the younger-subgroup effect; the solid line is the published younger estimate. Both panels use equal units on the two axes."}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

sh_m <- shrinkage(fit, type = "combined")
sh_g <- shrinkage(fit, type = "interaction")
sh_sg <- shrinkage(fit, type = "subgroups")
m_row <- sh_m$summary[sh_m$summary$trial == trial, ]
g_row <- sh_g$summary[sh_g$summary$trial == trial, ]
sg_row <- sh_sg$summary[sh_sg$summary$trial == trial, ]
m_med <- m_row$estimate
g_med <- g_row$estimate
mu_A <- sg_row$estimate[sg_row$subgroup == "Younger"]
mu_B <- sg_row$estimate[sg_row$subgroup == "Older"]
mu_A_image <- m_med - pi_j * g_med
mu_B_image <- m_med + (1 - pi_j) * g_med

mix_density <- function(x, mean, sd, weight) {
  w <- weight / sum(weight)
  out <- numeric(length(x))
  for (i in seq_along(mean)) {
    out <- out + w[[i]] * stats::dnorm(x, mean[[i]], sd[[i]])
  }
  out
}

dm <- sh_m$draws[sh_m$draws$trial == trial, ]
dg <- sh_g$draws[sh_g$draws$trial == trial, ]
stopifnot(identical(dm$.draw, dg$.draw))
stopifnot(all(c(".weight", ".cond_sd") %in% names(dm)))

square_limits <- function(..., pad = 0.12) {
  x <- unlist(list(...), use.names = FALSE)
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  span <- range(x)
  mid <- mean(span)
  half <- max(diff(span) / 2, 0.05) * (1 + pad)
  c(mid - half, mid + half)
}

lim_mg <- square_limits(m_row$lci, m_row$uci, g_row$lci, g_row$uci, m_obs, g_obs)
lim_ab <- square_limits(
  sg_row$lci, sg_row$uci, y_A, y_B, mu_A_image, mu_B_image
)
n_grid <- 90L
seq_mg <- seq(lim_mg[[1L]], lim_mg[[2L]], length.out = n_grid)
seq_ab <- seq(lim_ab[[1L]], lim_ab[[2L]], length.out = n_grid)
f_m <- mix_density(seq_mg, dm$effect, dm$.cond_sd, dm$.weight)
f_g <- mix_density(seq_mg, dg$effect, dg$.cond_sd, dg$.weight)
grid_mg <- expand.grid(x = seq_mg, y = seq_mg)
grid_mg$z <- f_m[match(grid_mg$x, seq_mg)] * f_g[match(grid_mg$y, seq_mg)]

grid_ab <- expand.grid(x = seq_ab, y = seq_ab)
m_ab <- (1 - pi_j) * grid_ab$x + pi_j * grid_ab$y
g_ab <- grid_ab$y - grid_ab$x
# This change of coordinates preserves area, so the density values transfer.
grid_ab$z <- mix_density(m_ab, dm$effect, dm$.cond_sd, dm$.weight) *
  mix_density(g_ab, dg$effect, dg$.cond_sd, dg$.weight)

younger <- sg_row[sg_row$subgroup == "Younger", ]
z_dash <- c(younger$lci, younger$estimate, younger$uci)
iso_mg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(z_dash, function(z) {
  data.frame(x = seq_mg, y = (seq_mg - z) / pi_j, z = z)
}))
iso_yA <- data.frame(x = seq_mg, y = (seq_mg - y_A) / pi_j)
iso_ab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(z_dash, function(z) {
  data.frame(x = c(z, z), y = lim_ab, z = z)
}))
iso_yA_ab <- data.frame(x = c(y_A, y_A), y = lim_ab)

pal <- interactmeta_palette()
col_hi <- unname(pal[["navy"]])
pts_mg <- data.frame(
  x = c(m_obs, m_med),
  y = c(g_obs, g_med),
  kind = c("Published value", "Posterior median")
)
pts_ab <- data.frame(
  x = c(y_A, mu_A),
  y = c(y_B, mu_B),
  kind = c("Published value", "Posterior median")
)
zlim <- range(c(grid_mg$z, grid_ab$z), finite = TRUE)

panel <- function(grid, pts, iso, iso_hi, xlim, xlab, ylab) {
  ggplot(grid, aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
    geom_raster(interpolate = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low = "#FFFFFF",
      high = col_hi,
      limits = zlim,
      oob = scales::squish,
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#D0D0D0", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#D0D0D0", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_line(
      data = iso,
      aes(x, y, group = z),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "#7A7A7A",
      linewidth = 0.3,
      linetype = "22"
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = iso_hi,
      aes(x, y),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = col_hi,
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = pts,
      aes(x, y),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "#FFFFFF",
      size = 3.8,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = pts,
      aes(x, y, shape = kind, colour = kind),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 2.6
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c("Published value" = 15, "Posterior median" = 18)
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c("Published value" = "#000000", "Posterior median" = col_hi)
    ) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    interactmeta_theme_report(variant = "minimal") +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(6, 8, 6, 6, unit = "pt")) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = xlim, ylim = xlim, expand = FALSE)
}

p_mg <- panel(
  grid_mg, pts_mg, iso_mg, iso_yA, lim_mg,
  xlab = "Combined effect, m",
  ylab = "Interaction, g"
)
p_ab <- panel(
  grid_ab, pts_ab, iso_ab, iso_yA_ab, lim_ab,
  xlab = "Younger subgroup effect",
  ylab = "Older subgroup effect"
)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(p_mg$coordinates$ratio, 1)))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(p_ab$coordinates$ratio, 1)))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(p_mg$coordinates$limits$x, p_mg$coordinates$limits$y)))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(p_ab$coordinates$limits$x, p_ab$coordinates$limits$y)))
p_mg + p_ab +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The shading is the posterior density, not a single summary. The square
and the diamond are points: the published value, and the posterior
median. Most of the posterior mass does not sit on either point.

ADVANCE's observed interaction is imprecise and is shrunk toward the
positive mean interaction estimated across comparisons. In this fit,
that shrinkage moves the posterior median to the other side of zero.
The published interaction in the Section 2 table is about $-0.311$; the
median of $g$ in Section 4 is about $0.311$. A sign change is not a
property of every comparison.

## 4. From that pair to the grey diamonds

The subgroup effects are the same linear map, now applied to the
shrunk combined effect and the shrunk interaction:

$$
\widetilde\mu_{Aj} = \widetilde m_j - \pi_j \widetilde g_j,
$$

$$
\widetilde\mu_{Bj} = \widetilde m_j + (1 - \pi_j)\, \widetilde g_j.
$$

The identities hold for the posterior of $(\widetilde m_j, \widetilde g_j)$.
They do not say that the median of $\widetilde\mu_{Aj}$ equals the
median of $\widetilde m_j$ minus $\pi_j$ times the median of
$\widetilde g_j$. `shrinkage()` prints the median of each transformed
subgroup effect. The next table compares that median with the image of
the two component medians. The diamond on the right is the printed
median, not the image.

```{r advance-shrink}
adv_sh <- shrinkage(fit)
adv_sh$summary <- adv_sh$summary[adv_sh$summary$trial == trial, ]
adv_sh

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    quantity = c(
      "Median of m",
      "Median of g",
      "Image, younger",
      "Image, older",
      "shrinkage(), younger",
      "shrinkage(), older"
    ),
    value = c(m_med, g_med, mu_A_image, mu_B_image, mu_A, mu_B)
  ),
  digits = 3
)
```

For ADVANCE the two calculations differ in the third decimal place. The
difference is the distinction between transforming the posterior and
transforming its medians. The credible intervals in the shrinkage
summary are intervals for the transformed subgroup effects.

The two subgroup effects are functions of one pair, so they are
dependent. A change in the combined effect or in the interaction moves
both grey diamonds. On the forest, each grey diamond is that
comparison's shrinkage median. When the introduction draws
incidence-rate ratios, it exponentiates this log-scale median. The
pooled diamond stays the mean subgroup effect at the reporting
information fraction. It is not this comparison's grey diamond.
